teaching.hint: How much of the robot’s route repeats after it has gone around the boundary once?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Every successful move advances one cell around a fixed perimeter cycle; position depends on distance modulo perimeter, but the initial and completed-lap states at the origin have different directions.
solution_outline.approach: Maintain total boundary progress modulo `2(width+height)−4` plus whether any move has occurred. Add each step count modulo the period; decode position and direction from the four edge segments.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The progress index identifies the current boundary cell, while the movement-history bit distinguishes initial East from post-lap South at index zero.
solution_outline.correctness: The corner-turn rule follows the same boundary cycle on every step. Thus accumulated modular progress gives the correct cell; inclusive segment endpoints preserve the arrival direction, and history resolves the origin ambiguity.
solution_outline.pitfall: At an exact full lap, reporting East at the origin confuses the completed-lap state with initialization.

common_wrong_turns: Simulate every requested step across all calls
Turn immediately on arriving at a corner
